doc.title: Sonny Igoe interviewed by Monk Rowe, Emerson, New Jersey, July 31, 2003

title: End of studio work and staff orchestras
summary: Staff orchestra jobs at CBS were cut; Igoe lost his in 1968, and he laments television's change.

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts
story.community_name: Working radio and television: network shows, studio staffs, talk-show bands

blocks.x: Well I just was wondering, when was your last studio date?
And was it a conscious thing, like I’m out of this now?

What happened to me with the studio stuff was that what happened to me with the studio stuff was that I would say it was in the 70s. Mid-70s. I had, we lost our jobs at CBS, NBC, ABC, all the staff orchestras except NBC. NBC still had “The Tonight Show.” That’s where Ed Shaughnessy was. They still had Johnny Carson and they had a big band as you know.

So they were the only ones who were still working. We all lost our jobs because every year the new contract came up and they cut 20 more guys, 20 more guys, 20 more guys. I got finished in 1968. I had 9-3/4 years at CBS. My severance was based on nine years. They wouldn’t give me the 3/4 year. Those companies—

Oh yeah. See that’s what happened to television. Television used to be show business. Now it’s situation comedies and car crashes and murders and all that kind of stuff. There’s no shows. How dare they call some programs shows? They’re programs, they’re not shows. A show is with a band and with dancers and singers and you know show people. It used to be run by show people. And then the lawyers and the accountants started to take over and we all lost our jobs and the whole thing changed. Now CBS doesn’t do a show, you do a show and sell it to CBS or NBC or whoever wants to buy it. That’s the way it works now. And there’s no staff musicians, that’s gone. Best musician’s job left is Broadway.
